To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the actinorhodin biosynthesis gene cluster is regulated by a complex network involving the actinorodin repressor, Atr, and a transcriptional activator, AtaR; and (2) the undecylprodiginine biosynthesis gene cluster contains an operon, the expression of which is controlled by the product of a single gene, redZ, that is not part of the biosynthesis gene cluster

the actinorhodiin, undeclyprodigiosin and methylenomyocin gene clusters contain genes that stimulate antibiotic biosynthesis specifically in the presence of extra copies of these genes, and that the expression of these genes is subject to negative autoregulation.

the actinorhodiin, undeclyprodigiosin and methylenomyocin gene clusters are coordinately regulated by the actIIORF1 and actIIORF4 genes and that actIIORF3 is the primary activator of the actI and actII gene clusters.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the genetic and environmental factors that control antibiotic production by S. coelicolor and related species, and with the regulation of the expression of genes involved in the biosynthesis of these secondary metabolites
the genetic and environmental factors that control the production of secondary metabolites.
the regulation of antibiotic production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
secondary metabolite production is a highly regulated process, the control of which involves a complex interaction between genetic and environmental factors.

antibiotic production is controlled by a complex interplay between the regulatory genes and their products and the growth conditions, and that the precise nature of this interplay depends on the organism and the antibiotic.
the genetic regulation of antibiotic production is extremely complex and involves the coordinated action of multiple transcriptional regulators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the actinomycete secondary metabolite gene clusters are controlled in part by the same mechanisms as are used for controlling the synthesis of primary metabolites.

the antibiotic production genes are regulated in two ways, one that is dependent on the presence of an inducing compound (e.g. methylenomycins) and one that is independent of the presence of an inducer (e.g. actinorhodins and undecylprodiginines).
the regulatory genes in the antibiotic gene cluster act as sensors of growth rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of secondary metabolism can be very complicated.
the genetic control of antibiotic production can be quite complex.

the antibiotic biosynthetic pathways of S. coelicolor are controlled by a complex network of regulatory genes, which are themselves subject to complex regulation by environmental and developmental signals.
